survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The chapter uses PISA 2000 microdata and reports that the PISA database includes a design weight that adjusts for non-response at the school level, which would partially reduce bias in prevalence estimates for low participation. The engagement indicators are constructed from student questionnaire items (sense of belonging) and absence-related items (frequency of absence, skipping classes, and late arrival in the two weeks prior to the survey). The analyses of country means and prevalence are therefore based on the weighted PISA estimates as provided in the OECD PISA database, while the multilevel logistic models used to estimate within-country school variation are described as null models fitted separately for each country. The text does not specify replicate-weight procedures (e.g., BRR/jackknife), so uncertainty quantification is presented via standard errors and confidence intervals rather than a documented replicate design.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This chapter does not report any plausible-value (PV) based cognitive achievement modeling; instead, it constructs engagement indices and dichotomous benchmarks (low sense of belonging and low participation) from questionnaire and attendance-related items. Because the dependent variables are engagement classifications rather than PV-based achievement scores, PV handling is not applicable. The chapter also does not describe an explicit missing-data strategy for the engagement items (e.g., imputation vs. exclusion), so missing-data handling is treated as a reporting gap.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The chapter uses PISA 2000 data for 15-year-olds across 42 participating countries (OECD and non-OECD). Engagement outcomes are constructed for all students with available responses to the sense-of-belonging items and the participation/absence items (absence, skipping classes, and late arrival during the two weeks prior to the survey). Low sense of belonging is defined using a cut-point on the unstandardised sense-of-belonging scale (below 3.0), and low participation is defined using a cut-point on the unstandardised participation/absence scale (<=10). The text does not specify additional analytic exclusions beyond the engagement cut-point definitions and the use of PISA design weights to adjust for school-level non-response.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD chapter analyzes student engagement in PISA 2000 using two engagement dimensions: sense of belonging (six questionnaire items about acceptance and loneliness) and participation (absence, class-skipping, and late arrival in the two weeks prior to the survey). It constructs dichotomous benchmarks for “low sense of belonging” (below 3.0 on the unstandardised scale) and “low participation” (<=10 on the unstandardised participation scale), and reports prevalence, country means (OECD average fixed at 500 with SD=100), and within-country school variation. The chapter uses multilevel logistic regression null models to estimate how prevalence of disaffection varies among schools within each country, and it also reports multilevel correlations between engagement and literacy outcomes in a subsequent chapter. Key results show that about one in four OECD students are classified as having low sense of belonging and about one in five have low participation, with higher prevalence in non-OECD countries. The analysis is cross-sectional and does not support causal claims about whether engagement precedes literacy performance; it also does not document a missing-data strategy for engagement items.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This is an OECD report chapter that primarily provides descriptive and correlational/multilevel modeling results for engagement indicators and their associations with literacy and school/family factors, rather than training or evaluating machine-learning predictive models. As a result, fields related to ML techniques and PV-based achievement prediction are intentionally empty or not applicable. The chapter also does not provide a detailed missing-data handling protocol for engagement item responses, so missing-data handling is marked as not reported.
